findings_addressed.oracle: A _BlockingLengthDoc holds the state lock inside set_document for a measurable interval. While the lock is held, both set_display_mode_state('hex32_le') and get_display_mode() are launched in separate threads. After 50 ms, get_display_mode() must NOT have returned (assert not getter_returned.is_set()). This creates genuine concurrent lock contention — not the earlier serialised set→notify→callback pattern that never produced an overlapping critical section.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: Remove 'with self._lock:' from get_display_mode() so it reads self._display_mode directly without waiting for the lock. Without the lock, get_display_mode() returns immediately while set_document still holds the lock, so getter_returned.is_set() is True after 50 ms and the assertion 'assert not getter_returned.is_set()' fails.

findings_addressed.oracle: Independent oracle: doc_a is always installed at Path('a.bin') with a fixed length of 999; doc_b is always installed at Path('b.bin') with a fixed length of 42. The test uses _BlockingLengthDoc to hold the state lock while an interloper thread races to install doc_b (and is itself blocked). After both threads join, every DOCUMENT_OPENED event is checked: the event for 'a.bin' must have size==999 and the event for 'b.bin' must have size==42. The old test only checked event_size in {1024, 4096} which can never fail regardless of which document's length was recorded.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In set_document, change 'doc_len = length_fn()' (called on local parameter 'document') to read length from self._document BEFORE the self._document = document assignment, e.g. 'doc_len = getattr(self._document, "length", lambda: 0)()'. This causes the event for 'a.bin' to report the previously installed document's length instead of 999, failing the assertion opened.get(str(path_a)) == 999.

notes: Both tests were rehardened to eliminate the serialised-execution weakness. test_concurrent_set_get_display_mode_observes_consistent_values now uses _BlockingLengthDoc to hold the state lock and verifies get_display_mode() BLOCKS while the lock is held — a genuine concurrent critical-section overlap. test_document_length_in_event_matches_published_document now uses a path-to-expected-size oracle: doc_a at 'a.bin' must always report size 999 and doc_b at 'b.bin' must always report size 42, catching any mutation that reads length from the wrong document object.
